compound.name: carnosic acid
compound.one_liner: Lamiaceae-only phenolic diterpene; rosemary's antioxidant (E392) that oxidises to carnosol on drying.

biosynthesis.pathway: MEP/terpenoid (diterpene; GGPP → copalyl diphosphate → miltiradiene → ferruginol → carnosic acid)

occurrences.source_citation: Ghorbani A, Esmaeilizadeh M (2017) Pharmacological properties of Salvia officinalis and its components. J Tradit Complement Med 7(4):433-440
occurrences.database: Dr. Duke's Phytochemical and Ethnobotanical Databases
occurrences.note: Ghorbani 2017: 'The most effective antioxidant constituents of S. officinalis are carnosol, rosmarinic acid, and carnosic acid'. Not quantified in the EMA sage report as extracted. | Basis as recorded: ppm as listed by Duke (basis not stated per row; for 'Essent. Oil' parts it is ppm of the oil, 10000 ppm = 1 %) Basis (fresh/dry weight) not stated by the source; excluded from /compare until confirmed.

pharmacology.functional_notes: Food antioxidant use: rosemary extracts containing carnosic acid and carnosol are EU additive E392 [43].

processing_stability.note: Oxidised to carnosol (and rosmanol, isorosmanol) in the presence of oxygen after harvest and during drying [43].

compound.teaching_note: A drying-chemistry story: fresh rosemary carries carnosic acid, dried rosemary more of its oxidation product carnosol [43].
gaps: No human evidence for the isolated compound found in this pass.
Amount in sage not in EMA report; sage row rests on Duke + review.
